steps.text: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Stir in the garlic, and cook until the aroma of the garlic has mellowed, about 1 minute. Add the red curry paste, and stir for 1 minute more. Whisk in the peanut butter, brown sugar, chili powder, cayenne pepper, fish sauce, sesame oil, and coconut milk. Bring to a simmer, whisking occasionally, until the sauce has thickened and is smooth.

raw_recipe.headline: The Best Thai Curry-Peanut Sauce
raw_recipe.description: This sweet and spicy peanut sauce is made with coconut milk, creamy peanut butter, and thai red curry paste.
raw_recipe.name: The Best Thai Curry-Peanut Sauce

review.reviewBody: Super duper delicious. The mixture of peanut butter and red curry is divine. We gobbled it up. I used only 3/4 cup peanut butter, and that was the most I would advise using. I also used ancho chili powder instead of cayenne, I skipped the fish and sesame oils, and I used only two cans of coconut milk for a thicker sauce. I added in Thai basil and lots of veggies such as carrots, onions, zucchini, water chestnuts and those mini-corn things.

I can't give this a fair rating because I modified a few things, but for a recipe base, it worked fabulously! The things I changed were: curry powder instead of chili powder; cartoned sweetened coconut milk (Silk). I wanted to use this sauce for a chicken curry base, so I sauted bone-in skin-on chicken thighs that were first liberally coated in salt, pepper, and curry powder, then once browned I removed the thighs, and continued the recipe as normal using the chicken drippings. I added some roasted peanuts while everything simmered. The final result was incredible!
To make it vegan, I omitted the fish sauce and added some soy sauce plus the juice of half a lime. I also only made a third of this recipe as I only had one can of coconut milk. Turned out great!

I followed the recipe except used 1 cup of natural peanut butter because that's all I had. Instead of brown sugar, I used honey which was a great complement. I tossed the sauce on some chicken and zucchini. If you cook the chicken and zucchini together, drain out the liquid before adding the sauce, otherwise a lot of the flavor gets lost. I also added some cilantro to my chicken dish. The fish sauce really is key in bringing out the best flavor.

YUM! Can’t wait to make it again so I can have some, LOL. Let me explain... I made the curry sauce so I could make a curry that my husband could take for dinner while housesitting. He doesn’t eat much meat, so I made the curry with onion, red and green bell pepper, and chickpeas. As soon as he heated it up and tucked in, he texted me from the housesitting gig “GOOD CURRY!!” He can be persnickety about his curry - and he’s a very good cook on his own - so when he says that kind of thing, I figure I done good. I will make it again, maybe with some shrimp. This one’s a keeper!

This was pretty delish. I only had one can of coconut milk on hand, and it still made a lot of sauce. I added some lime juice to counteract the sweetness since I only had 1 can of coconut milk. Added freshly chopped basil and pineapple, and served it over chicken with basmati rice. Everyone loved it.

After reading a ton of the reviews, I dropped the coconut milk to two cans and the peanut butter to 2/3’s of a cup. Then, because we like the burn, added three teaspoons of the chili paste as well as a couple of splashes more of hot chili oil. Absolutely fabulous!!! The bonus is the sauce is great in the rice as well as the satay!!

Oh people, don't skip the Fish Sauce! I use Red Boat fish sauce and it is delicious. I skip the chili powder and use more curry paste and sriracha. If you have gochuchang, that would work nicely too. Personally, two cans of coconut milk is enough and 3/4 c peanut butter. Be sure to add some onion, carrots, peppers to taste.

One word: YUMMY! I was surprised at the depth of flavor I could get so quickly with this sauce. I halved the recipe, substituted the juice of one lime for the fish sauce and replaced the brown sugar with about 1/4 cup honey and 2 packets of Truvia to reduce the calories a bit. So fast, easy, and DELICIOUS! I will make this again and again.
The flavor was very good. I think I would use 1 can less of coconut milk next time for a thicker sauce. I like to make it as a dip for Thai sticky rice.

This is a good basic recipe to jazz up. I found it bland even with the addition of lemongrass and ginger. Next time I will add more curry, garlic, ginger, lemongrass and tad less sugar. Maybe a dash of soya sauce too then a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds.

Served over sauteed red and green pepers, onion, diced tomato, cooked chicken and spaghetti. Yum.

This was a fantastic sauce with a few modifications for a smaller dinner. I reduces the brown sugar, peanut butter and coconut milk by 1/3, then reduced the rest by half and it turned out nice and spicy which is what we prefer. After the sauce was reduced by about half, I cooked my Chilean sea bass fillets in the sauce for 4 minutes a side, spooning the sauce over the fish as it cooked. Yum Yum Yum!
Maybe I didn’t reduce the recipe proportionately but I thought it was bland.
This was amazing! I didn't have red curry paste so I used 2 heaping tablespoons of regular curry and more cayenne pepper. Thank you for a delicious recipe!
My picky-eater ,33yr old son loved this recipe! it is better then our goto Taste of Thai Peanut curry sauce!
The sauce was too thick, and didn't have the same flavor profile as in restaurants .
It was perfect!! It’s just like the Asian restaurant’s peanut dressing I adore.

I only had yellow curry and regular sugar. It was still really good, I used natural peanut butter which I would most definitely recommend. I added super Thai hot chili and a squeeze of half a lime before serving with pad Thai noodles. It was good!
Modified the amounts of spices and peanut butter to taste. Great recipe, my family loved it.

This recipe was the one that introduced me to the website, so there is no doubt in saying that it must have been amazing if I was craving something and my high expectations were met. 
I found it best to read the comments before cooking, to ensure I made the best rendition of this dish to fix any of the less popular flavors.
I ended up doubling the recipe, only adding a third of the doubled amount of peanut butter; which was chunky instead of smooth. I added an accidental unknown amount of the curry paste (which was great), along with another accidental teaspoon of sesame oil (great again) in addition to the two teaspoons already called for when doubling the recipe. 
It saved well, but when chilled over night it became a peanut butter consistency before being heated back up in a sauce pan.
WASH YOUR DISHES WELL!!!!!
